Question: what motor should I buy for the replacement so that it fits? It is a relatively new part, so these "must" still be manufactured. I think this piece is Lego though because the plastic is hard and good quality like Lego, and it's the exact same colour as dark bluish grey. title: Identifying a Technic set by its blue pneumatic pump and 8-tooth gear assembly

Near the base, there is also a clear pneumatic cylinder connected via short black rubber hoses to a 3-port control valve. Everything points to an early-to-mid 1990s set, but I can't find a matching chassis diagram in the instruction archives for the standard pneumatic supercars of that era. title: Identify vintage clone-brand
body: I just received a bag of vintage clone-brand bricks. Never seen this particular type of brick before. Can someone identify them? They are supposedly (not sure) from the 70's or even older than that. Material feels lighter and harder than real Lego. It appears more brittle. About 1 in 10 bricks has a piece of sidewall broken off. Only have 2x2 (about 20), 4x2 (about 60) and 8x2 bricks (about 40) in white and red. And 1 window and 3 doors in yellow. Width and length are very close to corresponding Lego bricks, but they are about 1/2 millimeter higher. Injection mould spruce remnants are very visible on the inside of all bricks and protrude to some (varying) extend on most of them. No baffles/tubes. The studs are slightly smaller diameter than on Lego, but also slightly higher. Clutch power varies between half that of Lego and similar to Lego. You can put a Lego brick on top but it won't grip at all. The 2x2 and 4x2 have vertical slits on 2 opposing sides. These seem to give the bricks a little give making it easier to get them apart. The yellow window and door pieces have a little ridge on the side that slides in these groves.
